sources.title: FHA's Loss Mitigation Program
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
sources.authorityNotes: HUD's own borrower-facing summary of FHA home retention and home disposition options, raw HTML cached. No revision date is shown on the page. It summarises the options and does not list eligibility conditions or the length of the Pre-Foreclosure Sale marketing period; those live in HUD Handbook 4000.1 and Mortgagee Letters, which were NOT read for this guide. Applies to FHA-insured mortgages only.
sources.stalenessRisk: HIGH. FHA loss mitigation options are changed by Mortgagee Letter and hud.gov URLs were restructured recently (several older HUD URLs returned 404 on 2026-11-13). Re-read before republishing.

sources.title: Topic no. 431, Canceled debt – Is it taxable or not?
sources.authorityNotes: IRS's own tax topic, raw HTML cached. Page reads 'Page Last Reviewed or Updated: 24-Sep-2026', which makes it the most recent of the three IRS pages used. It lists the qualified principal residence indebtedness exclusion as limited to debt discharged before January 1, 2026, or under a written arrangement entered into before that date.
sources.stalenessRisk: HIGH. The treatment of canceled principal-residence mortgage debt is set by Congress and has an expiry date in the text. Re-read before every republication and in January 2027.

sources.title: Publication 4681 (2025), Canceled Debts, Foreclosures, Repossessions, and Abandonments (for Individuals)
sources.authorityNotes: IRS publication, HTML version, raw HTML cached. This is the 2025 edition, 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns'; no 2026 edition was available on 2026-11-13. Its 'What's New' states the qualified principal residence indebtedness exclusion is unavailable for discharges completed or discharge agreements entered into after December 31, 2025. Its 'Future Developments' note points to IRS.gov/Pub4681 for legislation enacted after publication.
sources.stalenessRisk: HIGH. Annual publication; the 2026 edition is expected in early 2027 and may differ. Statements about 2026 cancellations rest on a 2025-edition forward-looking note plus Topic 431.

sources.title: Instructions for Forms 1099-A and 1099-C (04/2025)
sources.authorityNotes: IRS's own instructions to filers (creditors), raw HTML cached. Page states 'Revised: 04/2025'. Written for the creditor, not the borrower: it says when a creditor must file, which is why the $600 figure is a filing threshold only.
sources.stalenessRisk: MEDIUM. Continuous-use instructions revised periodically; check the revision line before republishing.
